chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Is'haq! Fear Allah as if you can see Him, and even although you are not seeing Him, indeed He sees you. So if you think that He does not see you, then you have disbelieved; and if you know that He sees you and you present yourself to Him with disobedience, then you have made Him from the least significant of the observers upon you.'

key_terms.أَهْوَنِ النَّاظِرِينَ: The least significant of the observers

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between seeing God and fearing Him according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, establishing *khawf* (fear) not merely as anxiety but as a profound state of *muraqaba* (awareness of God's gaze). He delineates a hierarchy of spiritual states: denying God's sight constitutes *kufr* (disbelief), while committing sin with full knowledge of His observation reduces God to a trivial spectator, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the balance between divine omniscience and human accountability.
